analysis:
The supplied units cover head lines 1-797 of docs/architecture/inference.md. The only change in this file is at head lines 1030-1047, per the complete range map. That range is outside the supplied units. These lines therefore show unchanged context: the Nemotron Super slot, prefix bank scoping and GLM5Next admission.

The patch excerpt documents a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge. It reuses token IDs of rendered-prompt pieces per prefix-cache scope and states that reuse never crosses a cache scope. It uses ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates and has a load-time comparison against applyChatTemplate. Sampled background comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 is the kill switch.

Relevant threats are T-041 and SEC-035 (cross-tenant timing oracle). The new tokenization cache is a further in-process per-scope cache. Its tokenization speedup on reused pieces could add a same-scope TTFT hit/miss signal. That is consistent with SEC-035's accepted same-account residual, provided scope keying matches the coordinator-authored cacheSalt.

Integration must verify the following in PromptTokenCache.swift and LocalTokenizerBridge, which were not supplied:
(a) The cache is keyed by the authenticated cache scope.
(b) It is disabled when no scope exists, notably on the local endpoint and Nemotron slot paths.
(c) Memory is bounded (DoS risk).
(d) Template rewrites cannot produce token IDs that differ from the served template, e.g. special-token injection from consumer text cut at added-token boundaries (prompt-integrity risk).

This is documentation only. No concrete regression is evidenced in the supplied lines, but the implementation is outside the supplied evidence. The T-041 threat-model entry may also need a note on this new per-scope cache.
